notes: USMLE Content Outline 2026 page 33 was inspected directly and explicitly lists leptospirosis under Multisystem bacterial infections.
CDC Clinical Overview of Leptospirosis was updated June 2, 2026 and directly supports contaminated animal-urine water exposure, conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, renal failure, and systemic symptoms.
CDC Yellow Book directly supports prominent calf/lower-back myalgia and the contaminated freshwater exposure route.
Current CDC sources were used for all four distractors.

blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

option_audit.dengue: A real febrile-myalgia differential, but does not best fit the contaminated floodwater exposure plus conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, and renal injury.
option_audit.hepatitis_a: Can cause fever and jaundice but does not explain the characteristic exposure and conjunctival/calf-myalgia pattern.
option_audit.hantavirus: Rodent exposure is plausible, but HPS is defined by progression to pulmonary disease rather than this classic leptospiral hepatic-renal-conjunctival pattern.
option_audit.ehrlichiosis: A tickborne febrile illness with leukopenia/thrombocytopenia/transaminitis, not the floodwater/conjunctival-suffusion syndrome.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Floodwater contaminated by rodent material entering through abrasions, followed by fever, intense calf myalgia, conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, and AKI independently reconstructs leptospirosis.
adversarial_second_pass.dengue_attack: Myalgia and fever overlap, but dengue epidemiology and typical hematologic/rash pattern do not explain the full vignette.
adversarial_second_pass.hantavirus_attack: Rodent association alone is insufficient; absence of evolving pulmonary syndrome plus leptospiral hallmark findings makes HPS inferior.
adversarial_second_pass.hepatitis_attack: Jaundice alone is not decisive; the renal and conjunctival findings plus water exposure point away from HAV.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No antibody titer, PCR timing threshold, bilirubin/creatinine cutoff, mortality percentage, or treatment duration is asserted.
